comments.author: @Arionlappy
comments.text: Just throwing it out there for the person who said they have a list in their Notes app of presumably things they want to buy, that's actually a good thing. So I'm a recovering shopaholic, not really buying above my means but definitely buying to an extreme degree and buying things I didn't need. For years. I'm also a recovering hoarder. And there were a lot of things I had to do to break myself of the shopping habit but a huge element was delayed gratification. Don't just check out because you found the thing you think is SOOOO important. So I'd often make lists of things that would pop up that I thought I needed. And often times, I'd find something else that served the exact same purpose. Or my needs would change. Or I'd realize I didn't actually have that much money that month so it's good I didn't spend it. Or most of all, the impulse/adrenaline/dopamine whatever thing was happening that would trigger my INSANE need to shop, would fade. I'd look at the item on the list and wouldn't even be tempted by it anymore because the chemical reaction had passed. If I still want it 6-12 months later, then it's a much more reasonable buy. This works. I've waited 8 months for pants, a year for a specific phone, etc. It means I still shop, but I buy SO MUCH LESS than I used to. It feels like I'm free of the addiction.
